content.prompt:
Two circles of radii $3\text{ cm}$ and $11\text{ cm}$ have their centres $17\text{ cm}$ apart.

Find the length of the direct common tangent $PQ$.

answer.worked:
Draw $CH\parallel PQ$, meeting $OP$ at $H$. Radii are perpendicular to the tangent, so $HPQC$ is a rectangle: $PH=CQ=3\text{ cm}$ and $CH=PQ=x$.
$$\begin{align*}OH&=11-3=8\text{ cm}\\x^2+8^2&=17^2\\x^2&=225\\x&=15\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Same task as p43-q9: construct the rectangle (or right triangle) with legs 11-3 and the tangent, then apply Pythagoras with the centre distance as hypotenuse. Only the numbers differ.

answer.worked:

answer.worked:
The tangent squared equals the product of the external and entire secant lengths.
$$\begin{align*}TA&=5+15\\&=20\text{ cm}\\TP^2&=TB\times TA\\TP^2&=5\times20\\TP^2&=100\\TP&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Tangent-secant rule with the whole secant formed by adding 5+15, then a square root.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

answer.worked:
The products of the secant intercepts are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+5)&=3(3+9)\\x^2+5x&=36\\x^2+5x-36&=0\\(x+9)(x-4)&=0\\x&=-9\text{ or }4\end{align*}$$
Since $x$ is a length, $x=4\text{ cm}$.

classification.difficultyReason: Two secants from a point, with an unknown external segment. This gives a quadratic x²+5x-36=0 to factorise, and the negative root must be rejected.

content.prompt: These two triangles are equiangular. Find $x$.

answer.worked:
Equiangular triangles are similar, so corresponding sides have equal ratios.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{8}&=\frac{9}{6}\\x&=\frac{9}{6}\times8\\&=12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

For two secants drawn to a circle from an external point, the product of the external segment and the whole secant is the same for each secant.
